extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and patent examiners (practitioners handling appeals before the PTAB and USPTO examiners)
extracted.subtask_short: responding to new grounds on appeal
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards governing when an examiner's answer contains a new ground of rejection, how appellants must respond (reply brief vs. reopening prosecution), petitioning to designate a new ground, reopenings after appeal, substitute examiner's answers, and what factual changes do or do not constitute a new ground of rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments under 37 CFR 1.116/41.33 and non-new-ground treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment filed under 37 CFR 1.116 or 41.33 adds or amends claims and the advisory action indicates which individual rejection(s) from the action on appeal would be used to reject the added or amended claims, then (1) the appeal brief must address the rejection(s) of the added or amended claim(s) and (2) the examiner’s answer may include the rejection(s) of the added or amended claims; such rejection(s) in the examiner’s answer would not be considered a new ground of rejection within the meaning of 37 CFR 41.39.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: canceling a claim and incorporating its limitations into a dependent claim (or rewriting as a new independent claim) so that the appealed claim contains the canceled claim's limitations does not create a new ground if applicant was given fair opportunity to react and the advisory action advised which rejections apply. This provision does not change entry practice under 1.116/41.33 — those rules still control whether the amendment is entered; 41.39(a)(2) only permits inclusion of a rejection in an answer, it does not affect entry entitlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and treatment of 'individual rejections'
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'individual rejection' is a rejection identified by its statutory basis and the references/combination relied upon (e.g., claim 1 rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102 based on Reference A; claim 2 rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 based on Reference A in view of Reference B; claim 3 rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 based on Reference A in view of Reference C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When amendments combine limitations from different original claims, rejections that correspond to those identified 'individual rejections' (e.g., A in view of B) may be appropriate and not new grounds provided the applicant was advised in the advisory action that such rejections would be applied to amended claims. However, if an amended claim raises a new issue beyond those identified (i.e., a genuinely new ground), then the amendment may properly be refused entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing a different portion of a reference that merely elaborates (DBC example)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner’s answer cites a different portion of an applied reference that goes no farther than, and merely elaborates upon, what was previously cited, then such citation does not constitute a new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative case: In re DBC — Board cited an Example in a translation that elaborated upon the abstract's generic disclosures (same claim limitations) and the court held this was not a new ground because it 'goes no farther than, and merely elaborates upon, what is taught by the abstract.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing statutory basis (103 to 102) using the same teachings is not a new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner’s answer changes the statutory basis of rejection from 35 U.S.C. 103 to 35 U.S.C. 102 but relies on the same teachings of the reference(s), the change in statutory label does not constitute a new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative case: In re May — court affirmed that reliance on the same prior-art species supported a 102 outcome even though original rejections were under 103; 'lack of novelty is the epitome of obviousness.' The key is that the underlying factual/articulation of teachings is the same.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relying on fewer references but same teachings is not a new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner’s answer omits one or more references from an original 35 U.S.C. 103 rejection but relies on the same teaching(s) of the remaining reference(s) to support the rejection, this does not constitute a new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative case: In re Kronig — Board limited its discussion to fewer references but relied on same teachings and court held no new ground. The 'basic thrust' must be the same between examiner and board statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reordering references without changing relied teachings is not a new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner’s answer changes the order of cited references in the 35 U.S.C. 103 combination but still relies on the same teachings of those references, the change in order does not create a new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative case: In re Cowles — although the order of combining references was changed in wording, the examiner and Board relied on the same teachings; court found no new ground. Similar holdings in In re Krammes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considering other portions of applicant-submitted references to respond to arguments is not a new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner’s answer cites other portions of a reference that the applicant submitted (for example, to rebut a 'teaches away' argument), doing so to respond to applicant’s arguments does not constitute a new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative case: In re Hedges — Solicitor cited different portions of references submitted by applicant to counter the applicant's assertions; court held that searching references of record for disclosures pertinent to the applicant's arguments does not create a new ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition procedure under 37 CFR 41.40 (timing and effects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request to seek review of the primary examiner's failure to designate a rejection as a new ground in an examiner's answer must be made by petition to the Director under 37 CFR 1.181 filed within two months from entry of the examiner's answer and before filing any reply brief; failure to timely file waives arguments that a rejection must be designated as a new ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the petition is granted, a two-month period is provided for appellant to file a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 to reopen prosecution; failure to timely file that reply results in dismissal. If petition not granted, appellant may file a single reply brief under 37 CFR 41.41 within a two-month period. Extensions under 1.136(a) do not apply to the 41.40 periods, but 1.136(b) (patent apps) and 1.550(c) (ex parte reexamination) can apply. Authority to decide petitions under 41.40 is delegated to the TC Director or designee; no corrected examiner’s answer will be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant's options when examiner's answer contains a designated new ground (37 CFR 41.39(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner’s answer contains a rejection designated as a new ground, appellant must within two months from the date of the examiner’s answer either: (1) reopen prosecution by filing a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 with or without amendment/affidavits/evidence relevant to the new ground, or (2) maintain the appeal by filing a reply brief under 37 CFR 41.41 that addresses each new ground of rejection and follows brief requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reply under 1.111 may include amendments, affidavits, or other evidence relevant to the new ground and will be entered and considered (treats reopening as withdrawal of appeal). A reply brief may not be accompanied by amendments/affidavits/evidence; if it is, it will be treated as a request to reopen prosecution. If the reply is not fully responsive but is bona fide, examiner should provide time under 1.135(c) to complete it; if not bona fide and two-month period expired, examiner must sua sponte dismiss the appeal as to affected claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements and limitations for reply briefs when maintaining appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply brief filed to maintain an appeal must address each new ground of rejection per 37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(iv), follow other brief requirements (e.g., identification page and argument pages, each item starting on a separate page), comply with 37 CFR 41.41, and may not include any amendment, affidavit, or other evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reply brief may include new arguments responsive to the designated new grounds; however, arguments not raised in the appeal brief or not responsive to the examiner’s answer (including designated new grounds) will not be considered by the Board unless good cause is shown. Once a reply brief is filed, jurisdiction normally passes immediately to the Board and the examiner may not answer the reply unless Board remands. If a reply brief is accompanied by prohibited materials, it will be treated as a request to reopen prosecution under 41.39(b)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to timely reply to a new ground results in sua sponte dismissal
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant fails to timely file a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 or a reply brief in response to an examiner’s answer that contains a new ground of rejection, the appeal will be sua sponte dismissed as to the claims subject to the new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners normally will not make determinations as to the sufficiency of a reply to a new ground once jurisdiction passes to the Board. If the appeal is dismissed by the Board, the examiner should follow MPEP § 1215 for subsequent procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopening prosecution after appeal (SPE approval and considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may reopen prosecution after an appeal to enter a new ground of rejection, but reopening requires approval from a Supervisory Patent Examiner (SPE). In deciding whether to reopen, examiners and supervisors should consider the degree to which the rejection previously of record is being changed, any previous reopenings after the appeal brief, and the overall pendency of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office action containing a new ground may be made final if the new ground was (A) necessitated by amendment, or (B) based on information in an IDS under 37 CFR 1.97(c) where no 1.97(e) statement was filed (see MPEP § 706.07(a)). Ordinarily any after-final amendment/affidavit/evidence that was previously refused entry should be entered and considered when reopening; where multiple conflicting after-final amendments were filed, the first amendment should be entered and subsequent conflicting amendments not entered. Form paragraph 12.239 may be used when reopening prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options and fee consequences after reopening to avoid abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: After reopening of prosecution, to avoid abandonment the appellant must either (A) file a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 if the Office action is non-final, (B) file a reply under 37 CFR 1.113 if the Office action is final, or (C) initiate a new appeal by filing a new notice of appeal under 37 CFR 41.31 followed by an appeal brief under 37 CFR 41.37.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previously paid notice of appeal and appeal brief fees can be applied to a later appeal, but if fees have increased since payment the appellant must pay the difference. If filing a new notice of appeal, appellant must file a complete new brief in compliance with 41.37 within two months of the new notice. SPE approval is required to reopen prosecution (see MPEP §§ 1002.02(d) and 1207.04).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute Examiner’s Answer on remand and appellant response
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Board remands for further consideration of a rejection, the examiner may furnish a substitute examiner’s answer responsive to the remand. A substitute examiner’s answer responding to a remand may set forth a new ground of rejection, but any new ground in such an answer must comply with the requirements set forth in MPEP § 1207.03.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a substitute examiner’s answer is mailed, appellant must within two months either (i) request reopening of prosecution by filing a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 with or without amendment/affidavit/evidence relevant to the remand issues (treated as withdrawal of appeal), or (ii) maintain the appeal by filing a reply brief under 37 CFR 41.41 (if accompanied by amendment/evidence it is treated as a request to reopen). Extensions under 1.136(a) do not apply to the two-month period, though 1.136(b) and 1.550(c) may apply. A Technology Center Director or designee must approve substitute examiner’s answers (see form paragraph 12.285).
